rationale: C15 is a compelling drafting template. The child closely reproduces its sequence and much of its language: a statement of national importance; identification of fragmented or inconsistent federal policy; a call for comprehensive policy and organizational review; establishment of a Cabinet Committee; designation of a chairman, full members, and ad hoc participants; the identical offer of cooperation from the President's Advisory Committee on Government Organization; and a December 1, 1954 reporting deadline. C21 shares the Cabinet-committee letter machinery but is less closely parallel, while C19 shares the comprehensive policy-and-organization review structure without the same Cabinet composition formula.

shared_material.child_excerpt: To meet this need, therefore, I am establishing a Cabinet Committee on Transport Policy and Organization whose task will be the presentation of recommendations for my consideration.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To meet the needs to which I have referred above, I am establishing a Cabinet Committee on Water Resources Policy. The committee shall undertake an extensive review of all aspects of water resources policy.
shared_material.explanation: Both use nearly identical transition language to establish a Cabinet committee charged with a comprehensive policy review and recommendations to the President.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Because of your major responsibilities in the field of transportation, I am requesting you to serve as Chairman of this Cabinet Committee. By copies of this letter, I am designating the Secretary of Defense and the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization to serve as the other members.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am designating you the Chairman of the Cabinet Committee on Water Resources Policy. The Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Agriculture will serve with you on the committee as full members, and I am so notifying them by copies of this letter.
shared_material.explanation: The chairman designation and appointment of other members through copies of the letter follow the same drafting machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of the Treasury, the Postmaster General, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Director of the Bureau of the Budget will participate on an ad hoc basis. My Advisory Committee on Government Organization will be glad to cooperate wherever possible.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare and the Director of the Bureau of the Budget will participate on an ad hoc basis. My Advisory Committee on Government Organization will be glad to cooperate wherever possible.
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive shared language, including the same ad hoc participation formula and a verbatim cooperation sentence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Accordingly, I request that the Cabinet Committee on Transport Policy and Organization submit its recommendations to me not later than December 1, 1954.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Its recommendations for the strengthening, clarification and modernization of water policies, together with a suggested approach to the solution of organizational problems involved, are to be submitted to me not later than December 1, 1954.
shared_material.explanation: Both require policy and organizational recommendations by the identical deadline.
